text:
julia: hitting a weird JSON mode failure with pydantic coercion on our structured output. model seems to return a slightly malformed object when optional fields are null. stack: jsonmode + pydantic v1.10.6. error: "Failed to parse JSON: trailing comma at line 3"

julia: repro snippet below (shortened):
```
PROMPT: generate product metadata in jsonmode with schema:
{
  "type": "object",
  "properties": {
    "id": {"type": "string"},
    "price": {"type": ["number", "null"]},
    "tags": {"type": ["array", "null"], "items": {"type": "string"}}
  },
  "required": ["id"]
}
```

julia: model response (raw stream captured):
```json
{"id":"sku-123","price":null,"tags":["sale",],}
```

julia: pydantic parse error because of trailing comma after last array element + trailing comma on object. But in our local tests zod tolerated it in dev. customer sees failure in prod (Redwood hosted).

samir: can you paste the exact API call you used? are you using streaming? which model/version?

julia: using /v1/generate, jsonmode: "strict", streaming: true, model: open-llm-v2 (verified). curl:
```
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate -H 'Authorization: Bearer ...' -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{"model":"open-llm-v2","json_mode":"strict","prompt":"...","stream":true}'
```

elena: thanks — streaming + strict jsonmode will fail on small trailing tokens if the model emits an extra comma before closing. In strict mode we don't attempt to coerce. Is this from a canary dataset where tags can be empty?

julia: yes sometimes tags is [] or null. but the model occasionally emits an extra comma when tags is single element too. it's intermittent but reproducible with the above prompt set.

mike: quick triage: two possibilities — model output distribution (token-level) or our streaming chunk boundary merging logic. infra-bot: posted deploy logs showing no recent runtime changes.

mike: workaround options: 1) set json_mode: "coerce" (server will attempt to heal invalid JSON to conform to schema) 2) post-process streamed chunks and wait for final chunk then run a robust sanitizer (strip trailing commas) 3) pin model to a non-canary version.

elena: note: coerce mode can hide real schema regressions; for pydantic users that expect strict validation, coerce may surprise. Also different validators have different tolerance: zod tends to accept trailing commas in dev builds, pydantic/v1 does not. pydantic v2 changes behavior.

julia: customer expects strict validation — they want explicit parse error so they can fallback. but they also want latency <200ms. waiting for final chunk to sanitize adds latency. any suggestions to keep strictness and avoid extra latency?

mike: idea: enable prefix/KV cache + run a lightweight streaming regex sanitizer that only removes trailing commas in arrays/objects on-the-fly (cheap) then feed to pydantic. We can expose this as a toggle in jsonmode: "strict_with_sanitizer" to preserve semantics while reducing false negatives.

samir: open question: should we treat trailing-comma-only failures as a special class and return error code E_JSON_TRAILING_COMMA with suggestion to use coerce? would help clients handle programmatically.

elena: yes, return structured error codes. We already have E_JSON_SYNTAX but it's generic. We can add E_JSON_TRAILING_COMMA and E_JSON_UNCLOSED_ARRAY. annotate with "recoverable": true/false.

julia: I'll escalate to the customer with the explanation + workaround (set coerce or pin model). they prefer error code change and a short-term sanitizer toggle.

mike: I'll file an internal ticket to prototype strict_with_sanitizer + error-code variants. tagging infra and runtime to look at streaming boundary merge as long-term fix.

infra-bot: deployment-check: no recent model-serving infra changes in past 48h.

julia: thanks — marking this blocked->monitoring for customer. will update if customer requests coerce. :thumbsup:
